reader.humanQuestion: What does a ChatGPT pet actually do, and can it help me personally or is it only a decorative avatar?
reader.promisedPayoff: Tell a desktop reader which useful controls sit with a pet, what Mini does without an animal, and what a pet does not change.
reader.priorKnowledge: No knowledge of desktop apps, projects, Appshots, or ChatGPT task states is assumed.
reader.centralMentalModel: A pet is optional appearance around a desktop quick-chat and activity-control surface; the pet does not improve the chat itself.
reader.dailyLifeConnection: A person planning a birthday dinner can paste meal details into a small desktop chat while she uses another app.
reader.surfaceJob: A short dated reader explainer of OpenAI’s September 11 desktop quick-chat update.
reader.desiredFeeling: I know whether I want the desktop controls, the pet, or Mini, and I know when to start a project chat instead.

explanationPlan.plainAnswer: A ChatGPT pet is optional desktop appearance around quick-chat and activity controls. It can make those controls easier to notice while you work, but it does not make answers better; Mini gives the same controls without an animal.
causalSequence: OpenAI dated the desktop quick-chat update September 11.
On macOS and Windows the floating controls can start a typed or voice chat and show whether a thread is working, needs input, is ready, or is blocked.
A pet changes the appearance around those controls, while Mini keeps the controls without a pet.
A quick chat begins outside a project, so a reader who needs project context must start inside that project in the main app.
explanationPlan.workedCase: While planning a birthday dinner in another app, a reader can use the desktop controls to start a short ChatGPT chat and later open the thread when it needs her input.
explanationPlan.transferCase: If the same reader needs a chat to use a project’s saved context, she starts it from that project in the main app instead of from the floating controls.
explanationPlan.usefulAction: On desktop, choose a pet if you want the companion visible or Mini if you want only the controls; use the main app for a project-aware chat.
explanationPlan.formatSpecificStructure: The Story; The LAiDIES Read; What This Means for You; Cocktail Party; Class Notes; Sources.
explanationPlan.antiTemplateDecision: Do not turn a cosmetic setting into an AI capability story. Answer the decoration question early, then teach the single controls-versus-context distinction.

humourPlan.noneReason: The useful distinction is already memorable without turning the pet into a joke.

communication.surfaceAdaptation: Answer the usefulness question first, then make the invisible separation between an optional visual and the chat controls concrete in one ordinary personal task.

universalAnswers.plainLanguageIdentity: A Pet is optional animated appearance around floating desktop quick-chat controls.
universalAnswers.evidenceBasis: OpenAI’s Pets documentation and changelog were fetched and reread September 13.
universalAnswers.evidenceLimits: Only maker documentation is available; native runtime use was not tested and no universal availability or answer-quality claim is made.
universalAnswers.readerRelevance: A desktop reader can decide whether the floating quick-chat controls solve a small personal task and whether the pet itself adds anything.
universalAnswers.affectedPeople: The documentation names macOS and Windows desktop users, while web Pets have a more limited documented surface.

universalAnswers.readerAction: Choose Mini for controls without an animal and begin in the main app when project context matters.

model-tool-release.productRange: This is a ChatGPT desktop interface feature, not a model or answer-quality change.
model-tool-release.newCapabilities: The documented change is typing a quick chat from floating Pets controls and following threads from its bell.
model-tool-release.bestFitTasks: Small desktop requests while another app remains open, such as asking for a grocery list while planning a dinner.
model-tool-release.notFor: It is not an automation system, performance upgrade, universal availability claim, or project-context shortcut.
model-tool-release.nearestAlternatives: Mini keeps the controls without a pet; a project chat in the main app supplies project context.
model-tool-release.availability: OpenAI documents macOS and Windows desktop controls but says availability can depend on the account and workspace.
model-tool-release.freePaidBoundary: The reviewed documentation does not establish plan availability, so the article makes no plan claim.
model-tool-release.limitations: Pets change appearance rather than how ChatGPT completes tasks; quick chats begin outside projects; web lacks the desktop overlay and tray.
model-tool-release.technicalExampleProportionality: No benchmark or technical performance example is used.
model-tool-release.vendorEvidenceBoundary: All feature claims are attributed to OpenAI documentation and are not independent usefulness evidence.
